name: ntfy
description: Simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service. Send push notifications to your phone or desktop via scripts.
summary: ntfy v2.22.0 (released 2026-04-21) is the latest release, focusing on a security fix for an SSRF vulnerability in web push endpoint validation (GHSA-w9hq-5jg7-q4j7) and several web app bug fixes. Recent notable additions include S3-compatible attachment storage (v2.20.0), PostgreSQL read replica support (v2.19.0), verified email recipients via smtp-sender-verify (v2.21.0), and full PostgreSQL backend support (v2.18.0). The project is actively maintained with frequent releases. See the full changelog at https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases.

answers.What is the current license?: Apache 2.0 (server) and GPL-2.0 (clients) — dual licensed; check https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy for exact terms
answers.Is the project actively maintained?: Yes — multiple releases in March–April 2026 with active bug fixes and new features
answers.Does it support authentication and acces: Yes — access tokens, user accounts, and access control lists are supported

breaking_excerpts: v2.20.0: ntfy will take full control over the attachment-cache-dir or S3 bucket; files matching the message ID format (^[A-Za-z0-9]{12}$) with no database entries will be deleted — do not reuse the attachment directory for other purposes.
v2.21.0: smtp-sender-verify flag introduced to require email address verification before sending notifications; ntfy.sh now enforces this due to AWS SES suspension from unsolicited email abuse.
v2.22.0: Web push endpoint allow-list regex tightened to prevent SSRF (GHSA-w9hq-5jg7-q4j7) — previously unanchored patterns may have permitted unintended endpoints.

alternatives.name: Pushover
alternatives.review: Paid SaaS, simple API, iOS/Android apps.

alternatives.name: Gotify
alternatives.review: Self-hosted only, real-time push via WebSocket.

alternatives.name: Apprise
alternatives.review: Apprise supports dozens of notification platforms in one library but is a notification dispatcher rather than a pub-sub server, so it lacks ntfy's topic-based subscription model.

alternatives.name: Pushbullet
alternatives.review: Pushbullet provides cloud-hosted push notifications with cross-device syncing and file sharing, but has a restricted free tier and is not open-source or self-hostable like ntfy.

alternatives.name: Ntopng / Mosquitto (MQTT)
alternatives.review: Eclipse Mosquitto is a lightweight open-source MQTT broker offering robust pub-sub messaging but requires MQTT clients rather than simple HTTP, making scripting integration more complex than ntfy.
